description: Initial lazy-root benchmark harness compile failed because Nickel Context::eval_shallow() returns NickelError directly; added plan to map NickelError into local benchmark Error before rerunning.

Initial lazy-root autoresearch harness: added wide checked-in fixture, shallow discovery benchmark, eager selected-root baseline, and checks. Baseline medians show selected_root_total_wall_ns=72.4ms with current eager path forcing all 128 roots.

Selected-root force now uses a wrapper evaluation of only the requested record field instead of eager all-root extraction. Benchmark counts drop from 128/127 to 1/0 and selected_root_total_wall_ns improves from 72.4ms to 64.3ms while all_roots_total_wall_ns guardrail stays 38.9ms.

Reused one Nickel Context across discovery and selected-root force by importing the fixture through a synthetic session source. Selected_root_force_wall_ns dropped from 32.2ms to 0.27ms while discovery stayed ~32.7ms; selected_root_total_wall_ns improved from 64.3ms to 33.0ms with counts still 1/0.

Confirmation rerun of the shared-Context wrapper benchmark. Same code reproduced the big win: selected_root_total_wall_ns nudged from 32.98ms to 32.87ms, keeping discovery ~32.5ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns under 0.30ms.

Tried nickel-lang-core Program-backed discovery and selected-root forcing. Big regression: selected_root_total_wall_ns jumped to 127.7ms and discovery alone to 126.7ms, so Program::query/eval_full_for_export is much heavier than the current Context+wrapper path for this workload.

Tried refining the nickel-lang-core path to use Program::parse() for syntactic top-level record labels plus Program field selection for selected-root force. It crashed before benchmarking: Program::parse() panicked inside nickel-lang-core with `File parsed and then immediately accessed doesn't exist`, so this path is not stable enough for the loop.

Tried replacing eval_shallow-based discovery with wrapper `std.record.fields(import fixture)` via eval_deep_for_export, while moving benchmark/check scripts to a disk-backed CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Discovery regressed badly: root_discovery_wall_ns rose from ~32.5ms to 42.6ms and selected_root_total_wall_ns to 43.1ms, so deep export of field names defeats the shared-Context win even though force still stayed under 0.5ms.

Tried discovering root labels from the already-read fixture source string with Context::eval_shallow(source) while still forcing the selected root via the import-wrapper path. Mixed result: discovery improved to 31.6ms, but selected_root_force_wall_ns regressed to 3.47ms, so losing the old import-cache reuse made selected_root_total_wall_ns land at 35.2ms instead of the 32.9ms best.

Tried keeping the shallow root record alive and forcing only the selected field with Context::eval_expr_shallow before direct to_serde deserialization. Nickel only reduced the field to WHNF: CrunchDerivation deserialization failed with `invalid type: Other, expected: String`, so at least one derivation field still needs recursive forcing beyond a single shallow step.

Prototype public-API fast path: reuse one shallow root record, then lazily force only the selected derivation and manually decode simple string/array fields. It improved selected_root_total_wall_ns to 32.31ms with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.20ms, but the implementation only handled the benchmark fixture shape (no env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance) inside example support, so it is not general enough to keep yet.

Generalized the fast path into production seams: `crunch_eval::ShallowRecordSession` now keeps one shallow top-level record alive, and `crunch_glue::decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` recursively forces only the selected derivation fields. Benchmark improved from 32.87ms to 32.32ms total with selected_root_force_wall_ns down to 0.19ms, while new tests cover bad siblings plus nested env/inputs/fixed_output/provenance so the win is not fixture-only.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` so selected-root discovery can scan the shallow top-level record for count+target presence without allocating owned label strings on the hot path. Benchmark improved from 32.32ms to 31.97ms total while preserving root_count=128, selected-label validation, and the same lazy selected-root force path.

Made `ShallowRecordSession::scan_for_label()` use the shallow record’s O(1)-style metadata path (`len()` plus direct field lookup) instead of iterating every top-level field. That keeps the selected-root discovery API general while dropping selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.97ms to 31.25ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 31.06ms on the same 128-root fixture.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so benchmark path could reuse the selected Expr instead of looking it up twice. First compile failed because the new `SelectedTopLevelField` derived `Debug`, but `nickel_lang::Expr` is not `Debug`; fix is trivial, then rerun to measure whether the saved lookup matters.

Tried fusing discovery and selection into one `scan_and_select_field()` helper so the benchmark could reuse the selected Expr and skip a second lookup. Big regression: cloning the selected field Expr during discovery was much more expensive than the cheap presence probe, pushing selected_root_total_wall_ns to 53.9ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 53.4ms.

Added `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and stopped re-checking selected-label presence during discovery. The selected-root path now counts top-level roots in discovery and lets the force step own selected-field lookup, which dropped selected_root_total_wall_ns from 31.25ms to 30.42ms and root_discovery_wall_ns to 30.24ms without changing force counts or the 128-root guardrail.

Tried pre-scanning derivation records into a `DerivationFieldExprs` struct so lazy decode could trade repeated named lookups for one iterator pass. It regressed badly: selected_root_total_wall_ns rose to 32.38ms and selected_root_force_wall_ns to 0.23ms, so the extra top-level iteration and field collection cost more than the old direct lookups on this workload.

Tried caching `nickel_lang::Record` handles through lazy derivation decode so the hot path would avoid repeated `Expr::as_record()` calls and named-lookups would share one borrowed record view. It regressed to 32.98ms total and 0.22ms selected-force, so the extra wrapper plumbing and record-handle threading cost more than the old direct helper calls.

Tried precomputing a reusable `ShallowRecordSessionConfig` so repeated benchmark samples could skip re-deriving source-name and import-path metadata before each `eval_shallow`. It regressed to 32.69ms total and 32.48ms discovery, so cloning the prepared config each sample was slower than rebuilding those tiny path-derived values inline.

Tried caching top-level field count inside `ShallowRecordSession` so discovery would avoid a second `as_record().len()` after `eval_shallow`. It regressed badly to 43.34ms total and 43.05ms discovery; whatever borrow/layout/codegen change that added around session construction outweighed the saved lookup, so keep field_count computed on demand.

Tried making `ShallowRecordSession::field_count()` and `scan_for_label()` infallible now that the session constructor already validates top-level roots. That should have been a pure API/codegen cleanup, but benchmark cratered to 122.3ms total and 121.4ms discovery, so this reshaping clearly hurt optimized codegen on the hot path and is not worth keeping.

Tried a general simple-derivation fast path in `decode_crunch_derivation_lazy()` that detects absent complex fields (`env`/`inputs`/`fixed_output`/`provenance`) and decodes simple roots through direct `Record` lookups before falling back. It cratered to 73.10ms total and 72.44ms discovery, so the extra branch/helper layer hurt codegen far more than it saved on the benchmark’s simple derivations.

Tried adding `#[inline]` hints on hot `ShallowRecordSession` and lazy-derivation decode helpers to encourage cross-crate inlining across the benchmark path. It still regressed from 30.42ms to 31.18ms total, so the compiler’s default inlining choices were better than the forced hints here.

Baseline re-measurement at session start. Current best code from prior session (field_count + no redundant label check). selected_root_total=32.97ms, discovery=32.77ms, force=0.20ms. Prior session best was 30.42ms median — variance is expected across sessions.

asi.bottleneck: discovery is 99.4% of total — almost entirely Nickel eval_shallow cost
asi.force_status: 0.20ms is negligible, no room to optimize
asi.nickel_api: eval_shallow is the cheapest Nickel API (WHNF only), can't go lower
asi.prior_dead_ends: inline hints, caching field_count, precomputing config, fusing scan+select, DerivationFieldExprs pre-scan, Record handle caching — all regressed
asi.remaining_angles: Context::new() overhead isolation, import_paths Vec allocation, source_name String allocation, reduce fixture-independent per-session overhead, profile parsing vs VM eval split

description: Implemented isolated-worker bounded root forcing, streamed pipeline eval/convert into the worker, added parallel all-root benchmark coverage and captured the first parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns baseline bundle for the wide fixture.

Tried reducing parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated session per worker chunk instead of reopening a session per label. Benchmark run crashed before measurement because Cargo target dir `target/autoresearch-parallel-root` became unusable (`quote` failed with `E0463: can't find crate proc_macro2`) after prior test/build reuse.

Reduced bounded parallel all-root overhead by reusing one isolated EvaluationSession per worker chunk instead of reopening a worker session per label. Also switched autoresearch to fresh per-run Cargo target dirs to avoid shared-target corruption and benchmark contamination.

Reused coordinator-discovered root shape and labels inside IsolatedWorkerInput so worker sessions skip repeated shallow discovery before deep forcing. This trims bounded parallel all-root time slightly beyond the per-worker-session reuse change.

Tried pre-resolving requested labels to top-level indexes and skipping per-force label lookup inside worker sessions. That extra assignment/index plumbing regressed parallel_all_roots_total_wall_ns badly (281.6ms vs 113.4ms), so revert and keep the simpler worker-chunk session reuse design.

Applied the coordinator-derived worker metadata to the actual bounded parallel path: force_worker_assignment now opens worker sessions from cached shape+labels via open_worker_source instead of re-running shallow discovery in each worker. This removes redundant per-worker discovery before deep forcing.
